nodes.label: ticket-demo.svg (Static QR Ticket Fixture)
nodes.author: qrencode 4.1.1
nodes.rationale: Static raster-free QR SVG served from the Vite public dir so the demo preview can show a realistic e-ticket barcode on the payment-result screen without generating one at runtime. It is a design fixture, not production data: the payload carries an explicit invalid-use marker.

nodes.label: QRcode Group (29x29 Module Matrix, 3.92cm)
nodes.rationale: Single stroked path of 1x1 module strokes translated to (4, 4.5) inside a 37x37 viewBox: a 4-module quiet zone around a QR version 3 symbol, scaled with preserveAspectRatio="none" so it fills whatever box the ticket card allocates.

nodes.label: Agent Checkpoint Commit Protocol (issue #11)
nodes.rationale: Scoped checkpoints keep commits coherent, and only the coordinator commits so concurrent subagents do not race on the shared git index.

nodes.label: M1 Scope: Three Functions Only
nodes.rationale: Module M1 is deliberately limited to member registration, online ticket booking, and reward-point redemption; inventing further business behavior would break alignment with the bc.docx analysis diagrams.

nodes.label: DAO Layer with _fix Method Signatures
nodes.rationale: DAO signatures follow the _fix diagrams (taoHoaDon(hd, dsVe), tinhTongTien(dsVe, voucher?), kiemTraHetHan(idHoaDon), luuGiaoDich then luuVoucher) while dropping phatHanhVe, capNhatTongTien and timHoaDonTheoIdVe that no longer fit the design.

nodes.label: MySQL Schema: 13 Tables, 14 Foreign Keys
nodes.rationale: The canonical schema is 12 bc tables plus tblGiaoDichDoiDiem; derived values (tongTien, voucher expiry) stay out of columns and the duplicate tblVoucherGiamGia table was removed because the earlier 14-table count was a miscount.

nodes.label: REST API Envelope and Endpoint Groups
nodes.norm_label: rest api envelope and endpoint groups
nodes.rationale: All three endpoint groups use one {success, data, message} envelope and trust only server-side values; the client never sends authoritative customer id, price, points or hold deadline.

nodes.label: 300-Second Seat Hold with Server-Side hetHan
nodes.rationale: The hold deadline lives only in tblHoaDon.hetHan and the frontend clock is display-only, so a tampered browser cannot extend or decide expiry.

nodes.label: HttpSession as Server Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: httpsession as server source of truth
nodes.rationale: khachHangId is stored in HttpSession and KhachHang lives only in React state; no profile or password is persisted to browser storage, and the session id is rotated on login to prevent session fixation.

nodes.label: Ghe (Seat)
nodes.rationale: Sweetbox seats are selected as adjacent pairs, which is why they are modeled as two seat records rather than one.

nodes.label: GiaoDichDoiDiem (Point Redemption Receipt)
nodes.rationale: One receipt per successful redemption is the canonical history; a separate redemption-history table would duplicate the same event.

nodes.label: HoaDon (Invoice)
nodes.rationale: A pending invoice doubles as the seat-hold record, so PhienDatVe and GiuCho must not be modeled as separate business objects.

nodes.label: Use Case Catalog for Module M1
nodes.norm_label: use case catalog for module m1

nodes.label: Atomic Transaction Design (Reward Redemption and Booking)
nodes.norm_label: atomic transaction design (reward redemption and booking)
nodes.rationale: thucHienDoiDiem writes the GiaoDichDoiDiem receipt before the voucher and taoHoaDon saves invoice plus DANG_GIU tickets in one transaction, so any failure rolls back points, stock, vouchers, invoices and tickets together and no half-completed state is observable.

nodes.label: Business Rules R1–R12
nodes.rationale: R1–R12 are the mandatory, already-negotiated rules (points before voucher, one voucher per invoice, 300s hold, max 8 seats, Sweetbox pairs, derived totals) so implementation cannot invent or omit business semantics.

nodes.label: Q1–Q11 Architecture Decisions
nodes.rationale: Decisions were settled in grilling Q1–Q11: React+Vite replaces Thymeleaf, Spring Boot REST+DAO replaces a generic controller, a GiaoDichDoiDiem receipt is added, 3 QuaTang subclasses are kept over a split table, and 13 tables/14 FKs are fixed to stop the schema drifting from the analysis diagrams.

nodes.label: CINEMAN-DEMO Namespace Prefix
nodes.rationale: Leading token identifying the payload as a demo rather than a real issued ticket. The marker alone does not establish enforcement by a ticket-validation system.

nodes.label: KHONG-CO-GIA-TRI-SU-DUNG Invalid-Use Marker
nodes.rationale: Vietnamese 'không có giá trị sử dụng' (not valid for use) encoded inside the QR symbol. This identifies demo intent; it does not prove that a ticket gate rejects the payload.

nodes.label: Invoice Reference HD001
nodes.rationale: Invoice (hóa đơn) code the ticket belongs to; in runtime code the equivalent value is maHoaDon(hd.id) encoded into the QR.

nodes.label: Decoded Ticket Payload (CINEMAN-DEMO:HD001:VE001:VE002:KHONG-CO-GIA-TRI-SU-DUNG)
nodes.rationale: Colon-delimited ticket string: brand namespace, invoice code, one segment per ticket, then an invalid-use marker. Read by decoding the 29x29 module matrix (version 3, ECC L, mask 4).

nodes.label: Ticket Codes VE001 and VE002
nodes.rationale: One code per ticket (vé) in the invoice; the runtime generator uses maVe(v), while the demo fixture includes two ticket references.
